response.query: How to model spatial autocorrelation and spillovers (Spatial Durbin, spatial lag/error), choose clustering level for standard errors, and handle seasonal or nonstationary temporal heterogeneity?
response.answer: To model spatial autocorrelation and spillovers, use spatial lag or spatial error models. Choose clustering level for standard errors based on spatial autocorrelation diagnostics. Handle seasonal or nonstationary temporal heterogeneity with time-series adjustments.

results.title: How Spatial Autoregression works—ArcGIS Pro | Documentation
results.content: The tool can perform either a traditional ordinary least squares regression or one of the following global spatial regression models: the spatial lag model, spatial error model, or spatial autoregressive combined model. Second, the spatial error model can provide unbiased model estimates by accounting for spatial dependence in explanatory variables, such as the following:. The Spatial Autoregression tool can estimate three possible global spatial regression models, each of which account for spatial dependence in different ways. ### Spatial error model. ### Spatial lag model. Unlike the SEM, which views spatial dependence as a nuisance, the spatial lag model (SLM) incorporates the spatial dependence as an explanatory variable. The spatial lag model is used when the dependent variable has a large amount of spatial autocorrelation and exhibits a spatial spillover effect (meaning that changes in one area elicit changes in neighboring areas). In this case, the spatial dependence of the error term as well as in the spatial lag of the dependent variable are modeled. The SAC model can be used to identify spatial spillover effects in the dependent variable while also addressing the spatial dependence in the error term. The output feature class of the tool will contain fields of the dependent variable, explanatory variables, the predicted value of the dependent variable, residual and standardized residual, the spatial lag of the residual, and the number of neighbors of each feature. The spatial lag model reports an additional coefficient called Lag Y (rho). By default, the spatial lag model reports robust standard errors. However, after fitting a spatial lag model, a large amount of autocorrelation in the residuals may remain. The Anselin-Kelejian (AK) test is a diagnostic test that is used to determine if a significant amount of spatial dependence remains in the model residuals. Because the spatial lag model includes the spatial lag of the dependent variable as an explanatory variable, traditional linear regression prediction methods cannot be used. In the spatial error model, the regression coefficients can be interpreted similarly to those in standard linear regression. However, the SEM also includes an additional component, Lag Residual (lambda), which plays a crucial role in understanding spatial dependence within the model.
